name: Turkey & Zucchini Stir-Fry
pitch: A quick, savory weeknight hero — the soy sauce and garlic do all the heavy lifting here.
steps: Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add the ground turkey and break it up, seasoning with salt, pepper, and a pinch of garlic. Cook until browned, about 6–8 minutes.
Slice the zucchini into half-moons and toss it into the pan. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until just tender.
Drizzle in 2–3 tablespoons of soy sauce and a splash of vinegar, toss everything together, and cook for 1 more minute.
Serve on its own or over rice if you have it.

name: Garlic Turkey & Zucchini Skillet with Pasta
pitch: Simple but satisfying — this tastes like something that took way more effort than it did.
steps: Boil pasta (any shape you have) in salted water according to package directions — this is the one ingredient you'll need from your pantry or cupboard.
Meanwhile, brown the ground turkey in a large skillet with oil, plenty of garlic, salt, and pepper.
Dice or slice the zucchini and stir it into the turkey. Cook for 4–5 minutes until softened.
Drain the pasta, reserving a splash of pasta water, and toss it into the skillet.
Add a little butter and a spoonful of pasta water to make a light, glossy sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.

name: Spiced Turkey & Zucchini Lettuce Cups
pitch: A fun, hands-on dinner that feels fresh and a little different — great if you want something lighter.
steps: Cook the ground turkey in a skillet with oil over medium-high heat, breaking it apart. Season with garlic, cumin (if you have it), salt, and pepper.
Dice the zucchini small and add it to the pan in the last 5 minutes, cooking until just tender.
Add a splash of soy sauce and a tiny bit of vinegar to brighten the filling. Stir and taste.
Spoon the mixture into lettuce leaves to serve — butter lettuce or romaine work best.
No lettuce? Serve it over rice, in a tortilla, or just straight from the bowl — it's still delicious.
